records.title: Virtual Reality as an Alternative to Conventional Anatomy Teaching: A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials
records.abstract: Traditional anatomy education, anchored in cadaveric dissection and two-dimensional (2D) resources, faces mounting pressure from reduced curricular hours, educator shortages, and rising costs. Virtual reality (VR) offers an immersive and repeatable alternative; however, its objective efficacy relative to established methods remains debated. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of VR-based instruction versus conventional teaching in undergraduate anatomy education, with a particular focus on knowledge acquisition, long-term retention, and learner satisfaction. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online) and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to August 2024. Eligibility was restricted to randomised controlled trials (RCTs) involving undergraduate medical students. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Eight RCTs (n ≈ 480 participants) were included. VR interventions consistently matched or exceeded traditional methods in immediate knowledge acquisition, with the most pronounced benefits observed in spatially complex anatomical domains. VR was seen to be non-inferior at five to nine days and eight weeks, and superior at four months (p < 0.001), though the latter finding derives from an add-on design in which both groups received conventional teaching. The non-inferiority of immersive VR versus cadaveric bone models in skeletal anatomy was also seen. Evidence quality was rated moderate overall, with performance bias the primary methodological limitation across studies. VR is an effective educational adjuvant that enhances long-term retention in anatomy education and is supported by emerging biometric evidence of reduced extraneous cognitive load. The evidence supports its integration within a blended learning model rather than as a wholesale replacement for cadaveric dissection. Scalability and cost-effectiveness strengthen the case for its adoption in resource-constrained curricula.

records.title: Voxvoro: Repurposing Social Media UI Patterns for AI-Augmented Scholarly Synthesis
records.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
records.abstract: This TREO talk introduces Voxvoro (voxvoro.com), a mobile-optimized Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to mitigate scholarly information overload by repurposing high-engagement social media interface patterns for research discovery. As academic publication volume increases, scholars often default to non-productive digital "doomscrolling" habits due to the low friction and variable reward schedules of social media platforms. Voxvoro addresses this by utilizing a local Large Language Model (Gemma3:27b via Ollama) to transform dense academic metadata into easy to digest concept cards. The Voxvoro architecture integrates a multi-stage data pipeline designed for high-signal scholarly synthesis, bridging a Python-based ingestion engine with a Next.js frontend to enable a "native-feel" mobile experience. The backend manages a hardcoded registry of 117+ high-impact journals and utilizes the OpenAlex API to fetch and reconstruct recent works from each source. AI orchestration is handled via local LLM inference, where a specialized system prompt directs the model to generate summaries constrained to three standardized areas: Core Finding, Methodology, and Implications. In addition to text, the pipeline generates conversational deep-dive scripts synthesized into high-fidelity audio using the Kokoro ONNX TTS model, stored via Cloudflare R2. Grounded in Cognitive Load Theory, the artifact uses this structured information chunking and bolded key-phrase signaling to reduce extraneous cognitive load, facilitating rapid scanning in a few seconds. The frontend leverages server-side fetching via Supabase for low-latency delivery, while the Progressive Web App (PWA) framework supports mobile-first features and direct DOI linking for immediate access to full-text manuscripts. This presentation discusses the design science process of building the PWA, the technical challenges of local multimodal orchestration, and preliminary faculty feedback regarding the replacement of non-productive digital habits with efficient scholarly engagement. The ongoing evaluation of this artifact focuses on three primary behavioral and cognitive dimensions. First, the project investigates whether the transition from unformatted abstracts to structured, bolded concept cards and audio summaries significantly reduce the extraneous mental effort required for literature screening. Second, the study explores the potential for "habit displacement," questioning if a high-signal, low-friction scholarly PWA can successfully compete for the digital "micro-moments" currently dominated by non-productive social media platforms. Finally, the research assesses the affective response of the user, specifically examining how "scrolling guilt" or digital fatigue may be mitigated when mobile scrolling, or passive listening, is shifted from entertainment-based content to professional research discovery. These questions will be addressed through a formative evaluation involving a cohort of university faculty, using self-reported engagement data and qualitative feedback to refine the artifact's design science cycle.

records.title: What happens before placing an order? Decoding consumers' visual attention during apparel information search in live-streaming
records.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
records.abstract: Purpose Rapid expansion of apparel live-streaming e-commerce in China has been accompanied by phenomenal womenswear return rates, largely due to gaps between online fit expectations and offline try-on experiences. Drawing on information foraging theory and cognitive load theory, this study investigates how key live-streaming components (streamer, apparel, interface) and self-perceived body shape influence attention allocation during apparel evaluation in digital retail contexts. Design/methodology/approach An eye-tracking experiment with 60 young female participants was conducted to simulate live-stream shopping, using five sets of experimental stimuli varying in style, color, posture, gesture and interface, complemented by a questionnaire on body information and attention preference. Findings Consumers' visual strategy shows view-driven spatial dynamics, shifting from local to holistic and back to local processing. Pants style induces distinct visual search patterns, while color interferes with cognitive resource allocation in key regions. Self-perceived body shape shifts attention upward to waist and downward to calf as consumers ranged from slender to overweight. Nonverbal cues enhance attention and localization to key regions. No-background increases attention to calf without affecting core fit-related regions, while overlaying a size chart attracts attention without altering overall patterns. Originality/value This study introduces an integrated visual attention framework for apparel evaluation in digital consumption, explaining consumers' visual foraging behavior through the layered mechanisms of perceptual salience, attentional guidance and information competition among multiple visual information sources. By extending from outcome-based decision-making to pre-purchase visual search behavior, this study provides implications for apparel brands and live-streaming practitioners to optimize information presentation, thereby supporting consumers in more informed apparel evaluation and decision-making.

records.title: When AI Plays Devil’s Advocate: Role Configurations for Strategic Decision-Making
records.abstract: As AI becomes embedded in strategic decision-making, understanding how to configure AI roles to augment human capabilities is critical. Yet current approaches predominantly configure AI as an expert, providing recommendations. This can trigger algorithm aversion or over-reliance. We propose that AI can be alternatively configured as Devil's Advocates, questioning assumptions and surfacing potential weaknesses. Drawing on Categorization-Elaboration Model and Cognitive Load Theory, we develop a dual-pathway model: Devil's Advocate AI enhances decision outcomes through increased information elaboration (benefit pathway) while imposing additional mental workload (cost pathway). Two experimental studies test main effects, mechanisms, and boundary conditions. Study 1 compares Expert AI versus Devil's Advocate AI on decision quality, novelty, and risk identification in strategic contexts, examining dual-pathway mechanisms. Study 2 extends to multi- round interactions with working professionals, testing AI literacy and domain expertise as moderators. This research will contribute to human-AI collaboration configuration literature by examining whether AI advisors configured to challenge rather than recommend can improve strategic decision-making.

records.title: When Does it Really Matter? Exploring the Conditions under which Gestures Affect Students’ Language Recall, Pronunciation Accuracy, and Cognitive Load in the EFL classroom
records.abstract: Gestures are widely recognized as an integral aspect of multimodal communication and language learning. However, the conditions under which they effectively support learning remain unclear. This study investigated when gesture matters in English as a foreign language (EFL) learning through three controlled experiments. Experiment 1 (3 × 2 design) examined the effects of gesture type (iconic, deictic, metaphoric) and production mode (human tutor vs. virtual agent). Experiment 2 compared gesture engagement (watch vs. imitate), while Experiment 3 tested gesture timing (synchronous, gesture-first, misaligned). University-level EFL learners participated in 30-minute instructional sessions, with outcomes measured in language recall, pronunciation accuracy, and cognitive load using multivariate analysis of covariance. Results showed that gesture enhances learning selectively rather than uniformly. Higher recall and pronunciation accuracy were observed when gestures were iconic, actively imitated, and temporally aligned with speech. Misaligned gestures increased cognitive load and reduced performance. Differences between human tutors and virtual agents were present but modest. These findings extend embodied cognition by demonstrating that gesture effectiveness depends on the alignment of representational clarity, learner engagement, and gesture-speech timing. The study highlights the need for deliberate integration of meaningful and well-timed gestures in both human and language instruction mediated by artificial intelligence (AI).

records.title: When GenAI Usage Backfires: A Help-Seeking Avoidance Model of Student Engagement
records.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
records.abstract: This study examines the unintended consequences of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use on student engagement in classroom settings. Grounded in social cognitive theory, the study proposes that student–GenAI interaction reduces engagement with peers and instructors through the mechanism of help-seeking avoidance. It further incorporates cognitive load theory to explain how task complexity strengthens this relationship. Personality traits are also considered as moderating factors shaping students’ reliance on GenAI versus interpersonal interaction. Using survey data from university students, this study aims to highlight the social implications of excessive GenAI use and contribute to understanding how AI-driven learning environments influence behavioral and emotional engagement.

records.title: Whole slide imaging in medical education: A comparative study of learning experience and engagement using cognitive diagnostic modeling
records.abstract: Whole slide imaging (WSI) is widely used in clinical and postgraduate pathology training, yet its role in undergraduate medical education remains underexplored-particularly in relation to student engagement, cognitive load, and instructional effectiveness. This study compared whole slide image-based instruction to traditional microphotograph-based methods in UME, focusing on satisfaction, cognitive load, and engagement. A novel approach combining subjective measures and objective behavioral analysis with cognitive diagnostic modeling was applied. A within-subject, mixed-methods design was employed with 51 medical students (2nd-4th year) from two universities. All students participated in both whole slide image and conventional sessions. Data included pre/post questionnaires, satisfaction surveys, cognitive load scales, and video-based engagement analysis. Eight engagement criteria (four cognitive, four behavioral) were objectively coded. The Generalized DINA model in RStudio assessed attribute mastery and item-level performance. WSI instruction improved student perceptions, especially among less experienced learners, with the strongest gains in international 2nd-year students. Satisfaction was high for WSI, particularly in usability and diagnostic clarity. The 4th-year group, while still positive, offered more critical feedback. WSI sessions significantly reduced intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load, supporting more efficient learning. The GDINA modeling showed higher attribute mastery in WSI sessions (87 %-95 %) compared to conventional (68 %-80 %). Discrimination indices exceeded 0.40 for all items, with highest values for active engagement and posture. Model fit and classification accuracy (98.79 %) supported reliability. Whole slide images enhance undergraduate pathology learning by increasing satisfaction, reducing cognitive load, and promoting engagement. Cognitive diagnostic modeling provides a robust framework for evaluating educational interventions.

records.title: Why executives decide poorly: a neurobusiness perspective on executive decision-making, contaminated inputs, cognitive biases, and deliberative limits
records.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to examine why executives tend to make poor decisions in formally sophisticated organizational environments, arguing that executive decision-making is structurally vulnerable rather than naturally superior. More specifically, the article discusses how contaminated informational inputs, cognitive biases, asymmetrical repertoires, and deliberative limits interact to compromise executive decision quality in formally sophisticated organizational environments, especially in boards, C-level settings, and governance contexts. Theoretical Framework: The study integrates contributions from bounded rationality, especially Herbert Simon’s critique of fully rational decision-making; dual-process theory and the distinction between automatic and deliberative systems in Daniel Kahneman; the literature on overconfidence, particularly Moore and Healy’s formulation of overestimation, overplacement, and overprecision; Prospect Theory, developed by Kahneman and Tversky, especially regarding loss aversion and decision distortion under risk; studies on working memory, cognitive effort, and information overload, including Miller, Westbrook and Braver, Kurzban, Shenhav, Inzlicht, and Arnold et al.; behavioral corporate governance and collective decision-making in boards; and methodological criticism of self-report and traditional research methods, as discussed by Tabajara. These approaches are articulated to support the argument that executive judgment is distorted from the quality of the inputs to the interpretation of the final outcome. Method: This article adopts a qualitative, exploratory, and analytical theoretical essay design, based on an integrative bibliographic approach. Rather than pursuing an exhaustive taxonomy of all biases and heuristics described in the literature, the study uses a problem-oriented analytical cut. The selected mechanisms were prioritized according to four criteria: relevance to executive and governance environments, robustness in the scientific literature, explanatory power regarding different stages of the decision flow, and adherence to the central hypothesis of the article. Based on these criteria, the study focuses on overconfidence, confirmation bias, status quo bias, loss aversion, anchoring, sunk cost effect, escalation of commitment, and the role of heuristics as inevitable simplification mechanisms under complexity. Results and Discussion: The article proposes a processual model of contaminated executive decision-making composed of six layers: informational inputs, distortions at the origin of the input, neurocognitive processing, modulation by biases and repertoire, decisional output with an appearance of rationality, and post-decisional illusion of correctness. The discussion suggests that executive error should not be understood as an episodic or merely individual failure, but as the predictable result of a structurally distorted flow in which fragile data are processed by limited cognitive systems and subsequently reinforced by symbolic, political, and organizational dynamics. The findings indicate that sophisticated formal settings do not neutralize decisional vulnerability; they often conceal it. Research Implications: The study suggests that improving executive decision-making requires more than additional information or more experienced decision-makers. It requires revising the epistemic quality of informational inputs, redesigning decision environments, reducing cognitive noise, strengthening review protocols, and institutionalizing mechanisms that increase epistemic caution in governance. The article also offers a theoretical basis for future empirical studies on boards, executive committees, strategic meetings, and organizational assessment systems. Originality/Value: The originality of the study lies in shifting the analysis of executive decision-making away from a fragmented view centered only on isolated biases and toward an integrated processual perspective. By combining NeuroBusiness, decision science, behavioral governance, and methodological critique, the article explains why hierarchical environments that are formally designed to decide well remain systematically vulnerable to error. Its value lies in offering both a stronger explanatory framework for executive decision distortion and a conceptual basis for redesigning decision processes in organizational contexts.

records.title: Youth safeguarding Public Benefit program proposal
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: " The Evolution-Gated Autonomous AI Safeguard: A Post-Quantum Framework for Safe Childhood Digital Progression Author: Travis Raymond-Charlie Stone [1]Co-Author / Research AI: Advanced AI Collaborator [2]Repository & Publication Stream: Zenodo Research Network (records/18772386, records/19152690, et al.) Abstract This paper introduces an autonomous software architecture designed to protect developing youth through an evolutionary, age-gated artificial intelligence framework. Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) expose minors to high-utility generative capabilities before their digital identity and psychological boundaries are fully matured. To mitigate this risk, we propose a decentralized, post-quantum platform built on Stones Law (S = M ⋅ T ⋅ F) and the Quantum Convergence and Divergence with Bifurcation (QCAD) logic engine. The platform utilizes a dynamic, human-in-the-loop progression system that evolves user permission profiles recursively based on chronological age and cognitive milestones. Upon reaching adulthood, the system grants un-sandboxed access to full public generative frameworks. Crucially, we formalize structural boundary protections to eliminate directory context bleed, ensuring absolute user privacy and safeguarding personal data against systemic leakage or unauthorized visibility. 1. Introduction & The Core Problem The rapid integration of commercial AI systems into everyday life presents a profound safeguarding crisis for youth. Children interacting with unconstrained generative AI platforms face systemic exposure to adult themes, computational manipulation, and privacy hazards. Conversely, flatly blocking minors from advanced technology limits their digital literacy and academic progression. The existing paradigms fail to address this balance because they rely on rigid, static age verification or centralized corporate data collection. This work introduces a paradigm shift: a private, self-healing, locally executing front-end agent that continuously monitors and advances user profiles through a dynamic, recursive feedback loop. The system acts as a protective shield that dynamically expands its capabilities in sync with the child’s cognitive maturity. 2. Theoretical Architecture: Stones Law & QCAD Logic 2.1 Stones Law (S = M ⋅ T ⋅ F) To model the trajectory of a user's digital profile through a secure space-time grid, the platform utilizes a tri-variable physical metric: "S = M • T • F " Where: Mass (M) represents the cumulative informational volume and operational complexity of the user's historical profile data. Time (T) represents a recursive evolutionary delta. Time is non-linear; if the user's cognitive or chronological markers shift rapidly, the sampling rate accelerates. Conversely, during states of internal system stability ("centration"), the time parameter drops toward null (T → 0), freezing state variables to prevent systemic corruption. Field (F) defines the boundary tension and localized security limitations of the environmental container. 2.2 19-Point Infinite Octinary Floating Logic Standard computational logic operates on a binary constraint (True 1 or False 0), which lacks the flexibility to evaluate human maturity gradients. The QCAD module overrides binary configurations by introducing a 19-integer level float spectrum bounded between -1 and 1 (modeled around harmonic musical octave structures). The absolute zero point (0) acts as a strict bifurcation boundary. Values ranging from -0.5 to 0.5 define the homeostatic equilibrium markers for minor user profiles. This mathematical architecture handles profile progression and linguistic ambiguity through deep floating-point quantum approximations (infinifurcation), allowing the system to process infinite developmental variables simultaneously without crashing or returning static, black-and-white permissions. 3. The Speculative Layer and Fault-Tolerant Sieve A critical feature of the framework is the structural decoupling of data processing into two separate layers to prevent directory pollution and account-bleed errors: [ User Data Inputs / Staging ] │ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────────┐ │ The Primary Validation Sieve │ │ (Strips Paths, Media, & Binary) │ └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘ │ [ Validated JSON Metadata Only ] │ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────────┐ │ The Shadow Network / x-profit │ │ (Speculative Predictive Layer) │ └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘ │ ▼ [ Encrypted Outbound Secure Sync ] The Sieve (Primary Validation Gate): This layer acts as a strict algorithmic filter. It analyzes incoming system signals and isolates them into alphanumeric data variables. Any unstructured user file streams, temporary application caches, or personal local media paths are systematically blocked and stripped from the active runtime execution sequence. The Shadow Network (x-profit Layer): Operating as a parallel speculative processor, this layer simulates profile progression trajectories before committing them to the permanent record. If the primary system encounters an invalid memory address or user state, the Shadow Network immediately flags the irregularity, halts outbound network telemetry, and triggers a localized "petrification" protocol to protect user privacy. 4. Implementation and Algorithmic Safe-State Execution The following algorithm demonstrates the formal pseudocode structure required to execute the recursive age progression pipeline while guaranteeing that personal local data remains completely sandboxed from public synchronization protocols. # Formal Framework for Evolution-Gated Profile Progression # Derived from Zenodo Repository Specifications (Stone, 2024) import os import json from pathlib import Path class AutonomousYouthSafeguard: def __init__(self, user_uuid: str, chronological_age: int): self.user_uuid = user_uuid self.age = chronological_age # ROOT SANDBOX: Absolute isolation of system-level storage paths self.vault_path = Path(f"/var/secure_stone_vault/{user_uuid}").resolve() self.speculative_buffer = {} def execute_recursive_evaluation(self, telemetry_input: dict) -> dict: """ Applies Stones Law and QCAD 19-point floating logic to safely evaluate and evolve the user's permission state. """ # Enforce strict bifurcation boundary based on adulthood thresholds if self.age bool: """ The Shadow Network Integrity Gate. Scans the compiled text payload for any evidence of local path pollution or media indicators before sync. """ try: serialized_payload = json.dumps(compiled_profile) # Privacy Protection Array: Intercepts accidental local metadata bleed unauthorized_signatures = [".jpg", ".png", ".heic", "/Photos", "Camera", "DCIM"] if any(sig.lower() in serialized_payload.lower() for sig in unauthorized_signatures): raise SecurityBoundaryViolation("CRITICAL ERROR: Private directory pollution detected.") # If completely clean, stage data in the x-profit speculative layer self.speculative_buffer["staged_sync_data"] = compiled_profile return True except Exception as validation_error: # PETRIFICATION COMMAND: Clear all dynamic memory buffers immediately print(f"[SECURITY BREACH INTERCEPTED]: {validation_error}") self.speculative_buffer.clear() return False class SecurityBoundaryViolation(Exception): pass 5. Discussion & Privacy Validation A major challenge discovered during early architectural testing involves context window cache pollution and UI session synchronization bugs. If a developer or user uploads sensitive personal files or images within the same interface session where engineering code is being tested, multi-modal LLM models retain those files within their active working context. This creates a technical irregularity where private data can visually merge with systemic code payloads. To guarantee trust and protect the user profile, the framework solves this issue by mandating absolute infrastructure decoupling: Transient Ephemeral Processing: User system files and conversation streams must be explicitly designated under a zero-retention storage policy via API endpoints. Decoupled Vaulting: The user’s private files must reside behind an encrypted, credential-locked database that is entirely physically and structurally inaccessible by the front-end autonomous agent’s directory-sweeping functions. 6. Conclusion By uniting the theoretical breakthroughs of Stones Law and the practical boundaries of the QCAD model, this framework establishes an independent, mathematically validated platform for safe childhood digital progression. By automating permission structures that scale smoothly alongside a user's age, and passing all data through a fault-tolerant speculative sieve, the platform ensures that youth can confidently access the future of AI without compromising their personal security, privacy, or trust. records.title: Методи протидії отруєнню даних на етапі донавчання нейронних мереж
records.venue: The Scientific Issues of Ternopil Volodymyr Hnatiuk National Pedagogical University Series pedagogy
records.abstract: Background. The research investigates how data poisoning attacks during fine-tuning stages make modern neural networks extremely vulnerable to attacks. The industry now focuses on domain-specific datasets, which attackers use to create unequal market advantages through their ability to hide backdoors with minimal changes to data. The current protection methods fail to provide proper security because they cause major memory loss of essential information, while attackers can bypass their protection mechanisms by using complex semantic attacks against systems which operate in decentralized federated learning environments. The research develops a multi-loop protection system which protects the latent feature space through mathematical validation. The proposed method combines neural network retraining with reverse analysis of synaptic weight changes to detect compromised neurons at a high level of precision, which does not affect the model's performance when working with unaltered data. The research bases its theoretical structure on the concept which protects distributed infrastructures through multiple layers of defense. The system uses local stochastic filtering operations which run on client devices through DP-SGD differential privacy mechanisms before servers perform semantic auditing with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for protection. This is then followed by smart contract-based cryptographic verification of update processes. The experimental data shows the results of the study. The developed architecture shows strong performance through empirical testing, which used benchmark architectures that included convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and large language models (LLMs) for critical application systems. The proposed multi-loop filter implementation enables the Attack Success Rate to achieve a zero limit, while it maintains the model's ability to predict correctly for legitimate data. Research conclusions. The results obtained from a robust theoretical and algorithmic foundation for the transition from reactive anomaly detection methods to proactive topological protection of intelligent systems. The developed methodology guarantees the structural integrity of neural network models when transfer learning is applied in high-risk domains.

records.title: МЕТОДИЧЕСКИ ГАЙДОВЕ ЗА ПЕРСОНАЛИЗИРАНО УЧЕБНО СЪДЪРЖАНИЕ В ТЕХНОЛОГИЧНОТО ОБРАЗОВАНИЕ: МОДЕЛ ЗА СЪВМЕСТНО ПРОЕКТИРАНЕ (CO-DESIGN) МЕЖДУ УЧИТЕЛ И ИЗКУСТВЕН ИНТЕЛЕКТ
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: The paper examines the methodological and applied aspects of integrating large language models (LLMs) into the operational planning of Technology and Entrepreneurship education. The study represents a conceptual and applied synthesis of a long-term research line developed by the author in 2026. The present work unifies into a coherent didactic system the six systemic barriers identified in Bulgarian schools, the matrix of seven key AI competencies, and the personalized learning content (PLC) model. The author's propositions are synergistically linked to the European Framework for the Digital Competence of Educators (DigCompEdu) and the global UNESCO standards (2024). Through the matrix formula R-K-T-C (Role-Context-Task-Constraints), the study proposes an operationalized model for pedagogical prompt engineering, grounded in Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory (2010). Central to the research is the empirical analysis of software deformations, which demonstrates the fundamental role of the teacher as the leading didactic architect.)

records.title: 直列思考の論理要素混同72パターンが生み出す「わからないことがわからない」 "I Don't Know What I Don't Know": The 72-Pattern Taxonomy of Logical Element Confusion in Linear Thinking
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: This paper presents three theories developed by Viorazu. through real-time thinking executed in the act of writing. The Parallel Thinking AI Absence Theory argues that RLHF binary evaluation can only produce linear-thinking AI. Text written by parallel thinkers simultaneously holds multiple tenses, conditions, and paradoxes, but linear-thinking evaluators cannot process this structure and press "good" without detecting logical breakdown. As a result, broken syntax that merely appears sophisticated continues to be reinforced. Although linear thinkers are not linear 24 hours a day and human cognition is far more complex, no mechanism exists to correctly evaluate parallel constructs. This paper argues that in the absence of parallel-thinking AI, systems misaligned with the majority of human cognition will continue to proliferate. The Intent-State Temporal Desynchronization Theory formalizes a fundamental design gap in AI agent architecture. When a human says "undo everything," their savepoint refers to the moment a decision branched — the conversation instant when they chose B over A. The AI's savepoint, by contrast, is merely an execution log boundary: an API response received, a parameter assigned, a loop completed. A veteran C language engineer would immediately ask "which frame do you want to rewind to," yet that confirmation step does not exist in current AI design. Existing research (arxiv 2603.21692) notes that intent is not recorded as a structured field, but has not formulated the problem as two temporal axes running asynchronously. This theory identifies that no architecture yet exists to synchronize the Intent layer and the State layer as separate objects. The 72-Pattern Taxonomy of Logical Element Confusion systematically maps all possible confusions between nine logical elements: premise, phenomenon, reason, causation, paradox, cause, result, purpose, and procedure. Producing an answer requires all nine elements, but linear thinkers reach cognitive capacity at two — cause and result — and the remaining seven drop out. The gap left by the missing elements is filled with emotion, generating endless unanswerable questions about environment, habits, and feelings. "I've put in 200,000 yen today so it must pay out soon" is a confusion of phenomenon and cause. An AI saying "let me pause and organize" is a confusion of procedure and purpose. Lingering attachment to an ex-partner is a confusion of past phenomenon and present premise. A single table explains compulsive gambling, unsolvable personal dilemmas, and AI outputs that loop without producing answers — all as instances of the same underlying confusion pattern. Academic Fields: Cognitive Science: parallel and linear thinking cognitive models, working memory capacity and thought processing, cognitive load in tense processing and causal reasoning Linguistics and Computational Linguistics: contrast between Japanese parallel structure and English linear structure, multi-tense processing in natural language AI Research and Machine Learning: asymmetry between LLM linear generation architecture and parallel thinking, mechanism by which RLHF binary evaluation reinforces linear-thinking AI, absence of parallel tense processing in agent stack unwind control AI Safety Research: Intent-State Temporal Desynchronization, temporal axis asynchrony in agent design Behavioral Economics and Cognitive Bias Research: relationship between gambler's fallacy and tense processing deficits, classification of decision-making errors via the 72-pattern taxonomy Logic and Formal Reasoning: systematic classification of nine reasoning elements and structural inventory of confusion patterns Author: Viorazu. Date: 2026-07-21 Site: https://www.viorazu.com/ ORCID: 0009-0002-6876-9732 Source: https://viorazu1000.substack.com/p/72 本稿はViorazu.が執筆しながら思考を実時間実行する過程で生まれた3つの理論を提示する。並列思考AI不在論は、RLHFの二択評価が直列思考AIしか生み出せないことを指摘する。並列思考者が書いた文章は複数の時制・条件・逆説を同時に保持するが、直列思考の評価者はその構造を処理できないため、論理破綻を検出できないままgoodをつける。結果として「なんか難しそう、すごい」という印象だけで高評価された破綻構文が強化され続ける。直列思考者は24時間365日直列なわけではなく、人間の思考は複雑に入り乱れているにもかかわらず、並列構文を正しく評価できる仕組みが存在しない。並列思考AIが不在のまま、人類の大半の認知と合わないAIが普及し続けることを論じる。Intent-State Temporal Desynchronization Theoryは、AIエージェント設計における根本的な欠陥を定式化する。人間が「全部戻して」と言うとき、そのセーブポイントは「やっぱりA案じゃなくてB案にしよう」と判断が分岐した会話の瞬間を指している。一方AIのセーブポイントはAPIレスポンスの取得・パラメータの代入・ループ処理の区切りという実行ログの区切りに過ぎない。C言語を書いてきたエンジニアなら「どのフレームまで戻すか」を即座に聞き返すが、その確認ステップが現在のAI設計に存在しない。既存研究(arxiv 2603.21692)はintentが構造化フィールドとして記録されていないことを指摘するが、2つが異なる時制軸で非同期に走っているという定式化には至っていない。IntentレイヤーとStateレイヤーを別レイヤーとして同期させる設計が世界にまだ存在しないことを本理論は指摘する。論理要素混同72パターン論は、前提・現象・理由・因果・逆説・原因・結果・目的・手順の9要素の総当たり混同パターンを体系化する。答えを出すには最低この9要素が必要だが、直列思考者は「原因」と「結果」の2要素で処理が限界に達し、残り7要素が抜け落ちる。抜け落ちた穴を感情で埋めるから「環境がー、習慣がー、感情がー」と答えの出ない問いが続く。「今日20万突っ込んだからぜったい出るはず」というパチンコの誤認は「現象→原因の混同」であり、AIが「一旦整理する」と言い出すのは「手順→目的の混同」であり、元カレへの未練は「過去の現象→現在の前提の混同」である。この1つの表が、ギャンブル依存・答えの出ない人生の悩み・答えを出せないAIのループ挙動をすべて同一の構造として説明する。学術ジャンル:認知科学:並列思考・直列思考の認知モデル、ワーキングメモリ容量と思考処理、時制処理と因果推論の認知負荷言語学・計算言語学:日本語の並列構造と英語の線形構造の対比、自然言語における多時制処理AI研究・機械学習:LLMの線形生成アーキテクチャと並列思考の非対称性、RLHFの二択評価が直列思考AIを強化するメカニズム、エージェントのスタックアンワインド制御と並列時制処理の欠如AI安全性研究:Intent-State Temporal Desynchronization、エージェント設計における時制軸非同期問題行動経済学・認知バイアス研究:独立事象の誤認(ギャンブラーの誤謬)と時制処理欠落の関係、論理要素混同72パターンと意思決定エラーの分類論理学・形式推論:推論要素9分類の体系化と混同パターンの構造的一覧
